in patients admitted to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) for sepsis the adequacy of the initial empirical antimicrobial therapy is crucial in terms outcome, although early (<3 days) mortality rate was unaffected.
adequate empirical antibiotic therapy was independently associated with lower in-hospital mortality, whereas early mortality was unaffected by the adequacy of empirical antibiotic therapy.

in-hospital mortality was associated with the SOFA score at ICU admission, the increase in SOF A score during the first three days of ICU stay, and the administration of inadequate empirical antimicrobial treatment in patients with nonsurgical sepsis, whereas adequate empirical antimicrobials in surgical sepsis and urologic infection were protective factors.

the impact of adequate empirical antimicrobial treatment on mortality rate in a cohort of critically ill patients admitted to an ICU with sepsis, as well as the risk factors for administration of inadequate antibiotic treatment.
